page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor. This x86_64 architecture server features 32 dedicated physical cores running at 2.6 GHz with 1.0 thread per core. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and providing a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals distinct performance characteristics and tradeoffs. Single-core processing is a notable bottleneck, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the bottom 10% and Geekbench single-core scoring in the average tier. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by a Passmark CPU score of 31304.25 and average multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory performance also shows a stark contrast: while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 1393.35 GB/sec, uncached large-block read and write bandwidths fall into the bottom 25% at 35.41 GB/sec and 16.85 GB/sec respectively.

Given its high memory density of 256.0 GB alongside moderate multi-core CPU capabilities, this instance is structured for memory-bound workloads that do not demand extreme single-thread speed or high-throughput local storage. It is suited for database operations, caching layers like Redis, and memory-intensive enterprise applications. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and high RAM capacity provide a stable resource pool for memory-heavy tasks, though the weak uncached memory bandwidth and poor single-core performance represent clear tradeoffs for compute-heavy or sequential processing workloads.
